data.cultural_impact: The name Rāja holds significant cultural importance in India, representing power, authority, and leadership. It is a title that has been associated with various gods and heroes in Hindu mythology, such as Indra, the king of the gods, and RAMA, the ideal king and protagonist of the epic Ramayana. The term Raja has also been used to denote rulers and monarchs in Indian history.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, the name Rāja holds profound symbolic significance. It represents the ruler within, the higher self, or Atman, which is believed to be the ultimate authority and source of all power. The concept of Raja Yoga, one of the six major paths to spiritual enlightenment in Hinduism, revolves around the idea of controlling the mind and senses to attain self-realization and union with the divine. The king within us is our true nature, and it is our duty and responsibility to rule over our thoughts, emotions, and actions, just as a king rules over his kingdom.

historical_references.reference: Raja Raja Chola I, also known as Raja Raja The Great, was a Chola king who ruled from 985 to 1014 CE. He is considered one of the greatest rulers in the history of the Chola Empire, which was a major power in ancient India. During his reign, the Chola Empire expanded significantly, and he established the Chola dynasty's cultural and political hegemony over southern India.

Raj Tarangini, also known as the 'Rajas of Kashmir', is a Sanskrit chronicle written by Kalhana between 1148 and 1155 CE. It covers the history of the Kashmiri kings from the founding of the Kashmiri kingdom until the time of its completion. The name 'Raja' is used in the context of various Kashmiri rulers mentioned in the text.

modern_usage.modern_context: In modern usage, the Hindu name 'राज' (Raj) translates to 'rule' or 'king' in English. It is commonly seen in various contexts across three major platforms: 1) Indian Politics: Raj is a popular name for political leaders and parties, symbolizing the power and authority they hold. 2) Business: Raj is also a common surname in India and can be found in various business contexts. For instance, Forbes India's 'Richest Indians' list includes individuals with the last name Raj. 3) Entertainment: In Bollywood, Raj is a popular name for leading characters in movies, symbolizing the hero's power and rule over his domain. Overall, the name Raj carries a strong connotation of power, authority, and leadership in contemporary Indian society.
